flows.expected: One `tidy` advice item of 1 to 3 lines, the last naming cleanup.mjs tidy and the finding at docs/context/guide.md:3; no tidy item in the clean fixture

observations.actual: [AC:spec-11-1] passed (3/3 in the file): one tidy item, 2 lines, last line contains `cleanup.mjs tidy`, text names docs/context/guide.md:3; clean fixture gives []. The advice is produced by tidyAdvice in entry-check.mjs:36 and pushed into the wiring.mjs main output (wiring.mjs:186-191), the command the entry skill runs first (joycraft-entry SKILL.md:11,21).

Reviewer probes: P1 four findings still give exactly 3 lines (2 named, then "4 mapped doc lines name removed code: run `node .joycraft/runtime/cleanup.mjs tidy` ..."); P2 a removed symbol named only in AGENTS.md (entry file, report-only) gives no tidy advice; P3 a folder without Git gives no tidy advice and empty stderr.

flows.representativeInput: Same fixtures with and without the finding; this repository (feature/drift-tidy, 730 commits, 1004 tracked files) and a full clone with main moved to the root commit and on main
flows.expected: Same exit code with and without the finding; git status and file mtimes unchanged by the run

observations.actual: [AC:spec-11-2] passed: exit status equal with and without the finding; git status --porcelain empty after the run.

P5: the file snapshot (every path outside .git/objects with mtime and size) is identical before and after the wiring run, 28 files, and git status is unchanged; P6: a dirty working tree keeps its exact status. Start cost on a large repo: this worktree (211-commit merge-base range) 0.11-0.12 s per run vs 0.02 s for checkWiring alone; worst case (whole 730-commit history as the range) 0.15-0.18 s; default branch path (last 7 days / 100 commits) 0.23-0.25 s and it gave a real 3-line item. git status unchanged by every run.

findings.summary: Implementer-noted gap: the spec names the channel as `entry-check.mjs`; the advice function lives in entry-check.mjs (tidyAdvice) and prints through wiring.mjs, which the entry skill runs first. The brief decision start-advice = entry says "At most 3 lines through wiring.mjs", so this meets the brief.
findings.assumption: The spec parenthetical names where the function lives, and the brief decision names the printing channel; both hold.

That counterpart is not a declared verification input, so this subject does not bind it. The reviewer read the diff and the end-to-end tests cover it through wiring.mjs; add the path to the inputs if the coordinator wants it bound.

The repo's installed .joycraft/runtime/wiring.mjs, .joycraft/runtime/entry-check.mjs and .agents/skills/joycraft-entry/SKILL.md differ from payload/ (payload/PIN matches, spec-11-pin.log). Sessions in this repo do not see the advice until a reinstall.
The line says "which this branch removed from the code" also on the default branch, where the range is the approximate last 7 days / 100 commits (seen in spec-11-cost.log on main).
The dynamic import of entry-check.mjs is outside a try; tidyAdvice never throws, but a failing import (partial install) would make the whole wiring check throw instead of skipping the advice.

Range findings are net diffs: the whole-history range gave no finding while the 100-commit window on main gave 2, because a symbol added and removed inside one range nets out. Spec 3 territory; noted only.
